Title: Rulings Question - Form of Mist - Long Post

Messages.Author: TwitchBot
Messages.Body:
Ok, I know this is an issue that has probably been debated here
before, but I'm going to plead ignorance on account of not being a
regular reader of this group.....

I don't understand the logic behind the way this card is apparently
interpreted to work these days. I've read everything I can find about
it on the white wolf site, and I've talked with people here locally
about their interpretations, and I think I accurately understand the
way the card has been ruled to work. What I'm asking here is:

1)Is my understanding of the ruling correct? (Which I sincerely hope
I'm not) And if so,

2) Why in the hell did they do this, and do they recognize that they
have created a paradoxical ruling, that technically goes beyond the
rules of the game, and which renders the card not merely very
restricted in its utility, but literally impossible to legally play
(at superior by the acting minion) under any circumstance.

Anyway, here goes:

One of the "clarifications" that is posted on the white wolf web site
at http://www.white-wolf.com/, on the page titled "V: TES Official
Clarifications, Rulings, and Errata" most recently updated July 25,
2001; reads as follows:

"The superior form cannot be used by the acting vampire unless he
needs the stealth. [RTR 19970630] "

I had initially assumed that this simply meant that I can't play Form
of Mist if my stealth was already greater than the intercept of the
minion who blocked the previous action (which would bring up the
interesting question of how he blocked me if my stealth was greater
than his intercept, but never mind that). This assumption seems to me
to be SUPPORTED by the text of the Rules Team Ruling, to which this
statement is linked, which reads:

"10) You may play cards and abilities that provide stealth only if any
minions have attempted to block the current action, but not if the
acting minion's stealth exceeds all of those minions' intercept."

One or more minions did attempt to block the current action,
successfully I might add, and my stealth (apparently) does not exceed
the intercept of those (that is, the ones who blocked) minions.
However, my assumption is apparently not correct, based on what I've
read other places, although there is no actual explanation of why.

As the card is now written, when played at superior by the acting
minion, it counts as an action modifier, AS WELL AS a combat card. The
apparent logic of this decision is to prevent people from playing
multiple copies of the card on the same action.
This is fine in my opinion. It toned down a card that was probably a
bit too powerful. However, if this is all that was desired, this could
have been better accomplished by simply errating the card to read "No
more than one Form of Mist can be played on the same action." This
would not have crippled the card, or as I will argue, made it
literally impossible to use at superior by the acting minion.

Now then. It is ruled that you cannot play the card (at superior) if
you don't actually need the stealth that it provides. This is
considered analogous to not being able to play Lost in Crowds until
you need the stealth. This may be a valid analogy, depending on what
they meant.

The application of this is apparently that I can play my superior Form
of Mist only if there is an untapped (or a waked I guess) minion on
the table who currently has intercept equal to the amount of stealth I
had on my previous, already blocked, attempt at the action. Thus I
need one more stealth to get past the potential blocker, so I can play
Form of Mist to get past this.

However, this is very specifically an incorrect interpretation of the
rules, as posted on the white wolf web site. Here is why. The rules do
NOT state that you cannot play additional stealth on an action unless
there is a ready untapped minion on the table who currently has
intercept equal to your stealth. The rules state you cannot play
additional stealth until you are actually being blocked!

For example, if I want to bleed you with a vampire, and I naturally
have zero stealth, and you have an untapped blocker with zero or
greater intercept, that does NOT allow me to throw stealth on the
action when I announce it. Likewise, if I am bleeding you with a
vampire who has inherent +1 stealth, and you have an untapped blocker
with a sport bike, that again does NOT allow me to throw stealth on
the action when I announce it. I must attempt to bleed, then after you
try to block, then I can play my stealth to get past your blocker.

The rule in the rulebook upon which this analogy is based is in rule
6.2.2, second section, "Stealth and Intercept". It reads:
Stealth can be added to an action only when needed (that is, only if
the action is currently being blocked and the blocking minion has
enough intercept to block the acting minion).

Clearly, at the moment when you play superior Form of Mist, you do not
need additional stealth yet, because no block (of the continuation of
your action) has yet been declared. But then again, before you play
the card, there was no new action to BE blocked, and thus there could
not have been any attempt to block and thus no stealth needed.

This creates a paradoxical situation:

Player A cannot play Form of Mist because Player B has not yet tried
to block.
Player B cannot yet try to block, because there is not yet any action
to be blocked.
No action yet exists to blocked, because Player A has not yet played
Form of Mist.
Player A cannot play Form of Mist because Player B has not yet tried
to block.

Repeat ad infinitum.

Ok, so clearly we can't reasonably rule the card to work in the way
described above, because it is absurd. Lets fall back on the text of
the card itself. What does the superior version of the card say, as
errata-ed on the white wolf site?

"[PRO] Strike: combat ends. {When played by an acting vampire, this
card counts as an action modifier and the action continues} at +1
stealth as if unblocked (this action can still be blocked)."

What the card says is essentially: "Combat is over. Pretend nobody
blocked you, and add an additional stealth to your action." Now
normally, this is specifically not allowed. As we have already
discussed, section 6.2.2 reads:

Stealth can be added to an action only when needed (that is, only if
the action is currently being blocked and the blocking minion has
enough intercept to block the acting minion).

If we are pretending you weren't blocked, then under this rule you may
not add stealth to the action. If we abide by rule 6.2.2 then superior
Form of Mist simply may not be played at all. Fortunately we can fall
back on the rule 1.4.

1.4. The Golden Rule for Cards
Whenever the cards contradict the rules, the cards take precedence.
Clearly this rule tells us to disregard the violation of the rules
that is - and in fact has always been - inherent to Form of Mist.
Under this interpretation, the stacking limit of one Form of Mist per
action stays in place, because we are considering it an action
modifier. However, the card is still playable as it was clearly
intended to be.
To rule on Form of Mist the way that they apparently did, is to create
an new set of rules regarding Stealth and Intercept that are specific
Form of Mist, and totally different than the way they are applied in
the rest of the game, and which are contradictory both to the rules of
the game, and to any sense of logic.

Anyway, if anyone has any response to this, feel free. Maybe someone
in a position of authority wants to point out the flaw in my argument,
but I'm pretty sure there isn't one. What I really hope though is that
I've simply misunderstood the way this card has been ruled to work,
and we're already in agreement.

Thanks,

Matt Shields

Messages.Author: Joshua Duffin
Messages.Body:
mchir...@netscape.net (TwitchBot) wrote in message news:<ecf58b2e.01080...@posting.google.com>...

> Clearly, at the moment when you play superior Form of Mist, you do not
> need additional stealth yet, because no block (of the continuation of
> your action) has yet been declared. But then again, before you play
> the card, there was no new action to BE blocked, and thus there could
> not have been any attempt to block and thus no stealth needed.

This is where you got confused, I think.

When you play superior Form of Mist as an acting vampire, you
are currently being blocked. The combat you're in is part of
the action (if it weren't, there'd be no action to continue).
So you do have a blocking minion with intercept (almost always)

equal to or greater than your current stealth.

That's why you play Cat's Guidance after combat: the block isn't
over until the combat is over.

"If the action is blocked, then any card played to take the action
is burned, and the blocking minion is tapped and enters combat with
the acting minion (see Combat, sec. 6.4). Once the combat is resolved,
the action is over."

[rulebook, 6.2.3]

Josh

Messages.Author: Gomi no Sensei
Messages.Body:
In article <ecf58b2e.01080...@posting.google.com>,
TwitchBot <mchir...@netscape.net> wrote:

>However, this is very specifically an incorrect interpretation of the
>rules, as posted on the white wolf web site. Here is why. The rules do
>NOT state that you cannot play additional stealth on an action unless
>there is a ready untapped minion on the table who currently has
>intercept equal to your stealth. The rules state you cannot play
>additional stealth until you are actually being blocked!

You _are_ being blocked, though. By the minion you're fighting.

The problem seems to stem from your understanding of the block
and combat as separate things. They're not. To wit: Cat's Guidance,
which is played after the combat (but the vampire is still blocking),
and Freak Drive (superior), played after the combat resulting from
the block (but the vampire is still acting).

Since there is a blocking minion (the one you're fighting) with
intercept equal to your stealth (or the block wouldn't have
succeeded), it is legal to add stealth (via Form of Mist
superior, if one hasn't been played on the action previously).

>The rule in the rulebook upon which this analogy is based is in rule
>6.2.2, second section, "Stealth and Intercept". It reads:
>Stealth can be added to an action only when needed (that is, only if
>the action is currently being blocked and the blocking minion has
>enough intercept to block the acting minion).

All these conditions apply when your acting minion is blocked and
wants to play superior Form of Mist. The relevant blocking minion
with sufficient intercept is the opposing minion in combat (barring
tricky bits we won't go into here).

>Clearly, at the moment when you play superior Form of Mist, you do not
>need additional stealth yet, because no block (of the continuation of
>your action) has yet been declared.

There is no need, or indeed ability, to declare a block attempt in
addition to the one currently in progress (at the combat stage of
blocking).

>Player A cannot play Form of Mist because Player B has not yet tried
>to block.

Player B has successfully blocked and is in the middle of resolving
that block.

>Player B cannot yet try to block, because there is not yet any action
>to be blocked.

The action is still in progress while the combat resulting from the block
is ongoing.

>No action yet exists to blocked, because Player A has not yet played
>Form of Mist.

As above.

>Player A cannot play Form of Mist because Player B has not yet tried
>to block.

He sure can.

>"[PRO] Strike: combat ends. {When played by an acting vampire, this
>card counts as an action modifier and the action continues} at +1
>stealth as if unblocked (this action can still be blocked)."

Since it says the action _continues_, it is reasonable to infer that
the action never ended -- that is to say, Form of Mist doesn't create
a new action. It's more like moving a backgrounded process to the fore-
ground than it is like fork-and-exec'ing a new process, to use the
geekspeak.

>Stealth can be added to an action only when needed (that is, only if
>the action is currently being blocked and the blocking minion has
>enough intercept to block the acting minion).

These conditions apply. The action is currently being blocked (stipulated),

and the blocking minion has enough intercept to block the acting

minion (or the block wouldn't have proceeded to the combat stage).

So it's legal to add stealth. The only way to add stealth in combat
is Form of Mist, which also continues the action. Well, I guess
technically you can tap Opium Den in the middle of combat, but sans
a continue-action clause it won't accomplish much.

>If we are pretending you weren't blocked, then under this rule you may
>not add stealth to the action. If we abide by rule 6.2.2 then superior
>Form of Mist simply may not be played at all. Fortunately we can fall
>back on the rule 1.4.

With all respect (because you've put thought into this, clearly,
and you're a polite enough fellow), the 'pretend you weren't blocked'
thing is more your inference than the way the card actually works.
You don't pretend the block didn't happen. If you pretend the block
didn't happen, yeah, you can't play the card. But because the block
DID happen (and is happening right now, in combat), you can add
stealth, etc.

>Anyway, if anyone has any response to this, feel free. Maybe someone
>in a position of authority wants to point out the flaw in my argument,
>but I'm pretty sure there isn't one. What I really hope though is that
>I've simply misunderstood the way this card has been ruled to work,
>and we're already in agreement.

I think we are already in agreement. Let me know if I failed to
address something specific. I snipped bits pretty liberally and
didn't really indicate where, but let me know if anything fatally important
got cut.

gomi

Here's the thing. This generally only happens when the vampire is in
combat due to some other effect than the normal course of blocking
actions, which would be the small set of corner cases that Ken Shaw
refers to. The best example I can think of is Brujah Frenzy. A
Brujah (with PRO) is, say bleeding, and plays Alacrity for +1 stealth
after an attempt to block. The Methuselah being bled is unable to
intercept, and plays Brujah Frenzy, sending the bleeding Brujah into
combat with a vampire controlled by the acting Methuselah's
grand-prey. This minion in combat has 0 intercept, thus the acting
minion does not need the stealth, as he already has more than 0.

Xian

>>maneouver with a gun and deal damage, press, S:CE with Form of Mist at
>>superior, enter combat with B again, grin evilly at B:s controller and
>>maneouver to long dealing damage once more?
>
>Yep. Because the action was blocked in this fashion, Minion A needs
>stealth. So he can continue the action with Form of Mist (which can be
>played as any strike in the combat, not just the first or whatever).

[STUPID IDEA WARNING]

Hmm. Clan Impersonate Ellen Fence to Brujah Antitribu. Give her the
Sword of Judgement (preferably via Disguised Weapon).

She Rushes valuable tapped minion Democritus. Less-valuable untapped
minion Sir Walter Nash blocks. She strikes twice with the Sword,
presses with Flash, strikes once with the Sword and plays Form of Mist
to continue the action.

I see two or three cards' worth of setup, and two cards played during
combat. I like it. In addition, the additional strikes do NOT have to
be with the Sword, so you can always opt to strike-hands at some point
to make sure someone with low blood remains merely empty, as opposed to
torporized (making the Form of Mist impossible). If you're blocked by a
Raging Combat Minion, both cards revert to defense; maneuver to long,
Form of Mist to bail out. If people quit blocking, use Form of Mist as
a dodge at inferior; also usable against Piddly Minions with an Ivory
Bow. Include Blurs for when you actually want to torporize someone, and
all kinds of toolbox-toys as appropriate; you have plenty of room. Best
is a couple Shadow of the Beast, so you have a built-in press.

Include bunches of the CEL and PRO weenies to bleed for 1 lots.

-- Derek

"Because he's not me."

occurence

> Actually, just a few weeks ago I unleashed a !Tor/Tor deck that uses
> Catatonic Fear/Psyche!/Catatonic Fear/Telepathic
> Tracking/Riposte/Telepa... (you get the idea) on my local playgroup to
> S:CE the opposing vampire into torpor. It's pretty card intensive and
> hard to hone into a seriously competitive deck, but you should see the
> look of shock on your opponents' faces.
>

Some-one in my playgroup tried the the same thing but added Blood to Water
in the mix, and ,of course, a Walk of Flame to really finish the job.
Rebekka, Chantry Elder of Munich is the best vamp to try this with. the
others: Melisande and Bindusara, Historian of the Kindred but they have only
inferior tha. (add Tremere Convocation)

Very card and blood intensive (Ankara Citadel, Turkey!), but quite effective
against non-IG decks. Never sweeps because you almost sure to go through
your deck after your second oust (if any!).

Fun, nonethless

Jeroen
